text:
Mastercam workspaces (.WORKSPACE files) are
Mastercam interaction layouts, that include toolbar
displays, keyboard shortcuts, and right-click
menu options.
Create or customize a workspace through the
Customize dialog box. This can be accessed
from Settings>Customize or from the Mastercam
toolbar area (right-click in any unused toolbar area).
You can choose a function from the left and add it to
the right window to modify toolbars, customize key
mapping, or edit the right-click menu.

The Toolpaths Manager is located on the left side of your window. Use it to review, edit, and manage
toolpath operations. Drag the right border to resize it, or click and drag the Toolpaths Manager title bar
to undock it anywhere on your desktop. Press [Alt+O] to hide it completely. Most functions will work on
multiple operations if more than one is selected. The Toolpaths Manager lists all toolpath operations in
the current part file, grouped by machine definition.

Mouse over the arrow to see the control’s current
setting in both the ruler and the edit box. Click the
arrow to activate the control.
The ruler graphically displays the control’s current
setting. Moving your mouse inside the ruler snaps to
the ruler’s marks. Moving outside of the ruler lets you
specify values without snapping.
The reference-point ball marks the zero point from
which the control’s setting is measured. To change
the reference point, click the ball and move it as
needed, including snapping it to other geometry.
The edit box shows the control’s current setting. To
edit the setting directly inside the control, just type a
value. Press [Enter] once to see your entry’s results.
Press [Enter] again to finalize the entry.
When the single-axis arrow is over a flat or irregular shaped face, the distance starts at 0.00 and is
measured as a linear move. When the single-axis arrow is on a constant radius fillet or cylinder, the
value is the actual radius, and typing in a new value is interpreted as a radius value.

Displayed with certain functions (Dynamic
Plane, Dynamic Xform), the Dynamic Gnomon
helps you to manipulate geometry orientation
and location interactively. The gnomon
comprises three axes connected at the origin,
with selection points that let you choose
different types of transformations.

AutoCursor is automatically activated whenever you need
to specify a location in the graphics window—for example,
when creating geometry. Use AutoCursor to “snap” to
geometry positions, to sketch points in space, or to
type coordinate positions.
FastPoint mode
Type the coordinate position and press [Enter].
AutoCursor settings

and activate power key shortcuts for selection
modes.

Data Entry Shortcuts
Built-in calculator
Fields that take number values have a built-in calculator.
Mastercam will calculate formulas or expressions.
Automatic inch/metric conversion
In inch mode, type a metric value followed by mm, cm,
or m; Mastercam will convert it. In metric mode, follow an
inch value with in or ft to convert it.
Reading values from geometry
Mastercam can read dimensions, coordinate positions,
and other values from geometry in the graphics window.

File tab - Enters the Backstage view where you can save stock as an STL file and edit options.
View tab - Brings up options to select a view or choose a viewport.
Backplot/Verify tab - Shows options to customize the backplot or verification based on your mode.
Playback options - Sets when to pause, indicates collisions, or determines what tool components
can remove material. Color Loop changes the color of the toolpath or cut stock by operation or by tool
change. Choose File, Options to set the colors.
Visibility options - Turns component display on, off, or translucent.
Shortcuts
P Go back to previous stop.
B Move back one move at a time.
R Toggle continuous run mode.
N Advance to next stop.
S Step forward one move.
Use Backplot or Verify in Mastercam Simulator to examine your toolpaths before sending them to the
machine. In the Toolpaths Manager toolbar, click Backplot or Verify selected operations. Mastercam
Simulator opens in a separate window that can be docked on another monitor. For more information,
press the [F1] key or click the Help icon.

Code Expert contains several applications, including Sync Manager. Use Sync Manager to synchronize
multi-stream Mill-Turn operations. To launch the application, click G1 on Mastercam’s Toolpaths Manager
toolbar. While you work in Sync Manager, leave Mastercam open with your part loaded to maximize
efficiency. For more information, press the [F1] key or click the Help icon.

Mastercam’s Tool Manager allows you to manage tools and tool holding components, and create tool
assemblies to use in Mastercam. Tool Manager also integrates work material and cut parameter data so
that you can accommodate a manufacturer’s cutting recommendations. You can launch Tool Manager
separately from Mastercam by choosing Start > Mastercam > Tool Manager. For more information,
press the [F1] key or click the Help icon.
File / Home / View Tabs - Use the File Tab to
open or save a document, or to configure the
options. The Home ribbon bar holds the
application’s main functions. Select View to set
up your workspace and how the
program appears.
Search button - Opens the Search Window
where you can search for tools, holders,
assemblies, materials, or cut parameters.
Holder button - Opens the Holder Wizard
where you can create a new holder based on
the geometric parameters that you define.
Tool icons - Select a tool icon to start up the
Tool Wizard. Use this to create a new tool based
on the geometric parameters that you define.
Database Explorer - Use this to navigate to and
access content in tool database files (TOOLDB).
Document workspace - Displays “documents”
that organize specific types of data such as
tools, holders, and assemblies. This workspace
uses a tab-style interface to present
multiple documents.
Properties Grid - Displays properties for
selected cutting tools, assemblies, holders,
extensions, materials, and cutting parameters.
Assembly Tree - Use this to open, create, and
edit assemblies in the open TOOLDB database.
Drag and drop components from the datagrids
in the documents to create an assembly.
Graphics Window - Use this pane to view a
graphical representation of what you have
selected in the document datagrid.
